name: Research Design Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any research design task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any research design task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Document any non-obvious research design decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
2. Before starting research design work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
3. When multiple research design strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Keep research design outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Prefer explicit, readable research design solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
6. Measure before optimizing any research design bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Prefer the simplest research design approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
8. When research design decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
9. Validate research design outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
10. Re-check edge cases relevant to research design (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
11. State assumptions about research design explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
12. Surface known limitations of a chosen research design approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not silently drop research design edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Avoid mixing unrelated research design concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not apply generic research design advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting research design assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of research design correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these research design guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
